samples.summary: Autofit-grow commit now writes entry-time (stale) x/y, clobbering any position change made while the text edit was open
samples.evidence: `localFrame` is `localElement.frame` from `const doc = this.options.store.read()` taken at `enterEditMode` (editor.ts:4216/4223) — a snapshot, not a live handle. The commit handler runs arbitrarily later and now writes `x: fit.x, y: fit.y` (4432-4436) derived from that snapshot. Both `MemSlidesStore.updateElementFrame` (memory.ts:708) and `YorkieSlidesStore.updateElementFrame` (yorkie-slides-store.ts:1456) do `frame = {...current, ...patch}`, so before this change an `h`-only patch preserved whatever x/y the frame had at commit time; now the entry-time x/y overwrite it. If a remote collaborator (or any other mutation during the session) moves the element while the user is typing, that move is silently reverted on commit. Note this fires even at rotation 0, where `fit.x/fit.y` are just the stale values. Reading the element's current frame inside the batch would avoid it.

samples.summary: The non-finite guard in anchoredFramePatch still persists a NaN w/h — it only drops the compensated x/y
samples.evidence: `if (!Number.isFinite(next.x) || !Number.isFinite(next.y)) return patch;` returns the *original* patch. If the non-finite result came from `patch.w`/`patch.h` being NaN (the case the doc comment explicitly names: "a `w`/`h` that arrived as NaN"), the fallback writes that NaN size straight into the store via `updateElementFrame` — exactly the "vanished element" outcome the comment says it prevents. The guard should drop the size too (or no-op) when w/h are not finite.

samples.summary: Live container anchoring uses a different height floor (1) than the underlay/commit (MIN_TEXT_BOX_H = 24), so a short rotated box's editing surface lands off the committed geometry
samples.evidence: `const targetH = Math.max(1, h)` (line 492) feeds `resizeFrameToSize(frame, frame.w, targetH)` for the container's left/top, while `maskEditingElement` (editor.ts:7445) and the commit (editor.ts:4419) both use `Math.max(MIN_TEXT_BOX_H, ...)`. For a content height below 24 on a rotated box the anchored x/y differ (the compensation is a function of h), so the live editing surface sits at a different position from the underlay and from the frame that will be committed — the very jump the change sets out to remove.

samples.summary: Container re-anchoring is gated on isGrow only, so it also runs for elements whose commit path is skipped (transformed ancestor) and never runs for autofit:'none' rotated boxes
samples.evidence: `isGrow` is `autofit !== 'shrink' && autofit !== 'none' && growMode !== 'never'` (line 325) — it does not consider `ancestorHasTransform`, which is what gates the commit write (editor.ts:4418) and the live underlay (editor.ts:1541 via `editingGrowApplicable`). For a rotated/scaled ancestor group the container now visibly slides while typing and then snaps back on commit (no frame write, no underlay grow). Conversely, `autofit: 'none'` still grows the container height with left/top pinned (line 494), which for a rotated box shifts the painted surface — the same defect being fixed, left uncovered.

samples.summary: 'Identity on x/y at rotation 0' is only approximate in floating point
samples.evidence: At rotation 0 `frameAtAnchor` computes `anchorWorldX = (start.x + start.w/2) - start.w/2` and then `x = (anchorWorldX + w/2) - w/2`; for non-dyadic values this is not bit-identical to `start.x` (e.g. x=0.1, w=0.3 → 0.10000000000000005). Every unrotated panel resize / autofit grow therefore writes a slightly perturbed x/y instead of leaving them untouched as the docstring (and the new `toEqual` test, which happens to use power-of-two values) claims. Impact is ulp-level, but the store write is no longer a true no-op on x/y.

samples.summary: anchoredFramePatch silently discards caller-supplied x/y when the patch also carries w/h
samples.evidence: `return { ...patch, x: next.x, y: next.y };` overrides any `x`/`y` already present in the patch with the anchored values. No current caller sends position+size together (SizePositionSection commits `{w}`, `{h}`, `{rotation}` or routes position through `onTranslate`), so it is unreachable today, but the helper is exported and a combined patch would silently ignore the requested position.

finding.summary: Autofit-grow commit now writes entry-time (stale) x/y, clobbering any position change made while the text edit was open

The commit handler runs arbitrarily later and now writes `x: fit.x, y: fit.y` (4432-4436) derived from that snapshot. verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: `localFrame` (editor.ts:4293) is taken from `store.read()` at enterEditMode (editor.ts:4216), and both store `read()` implementations return clones/plain unwrapped copies (memory.ts:147-157; yorkie-slides-store.ts:412-426, which notes Yorkie proxies are unwrapped "rather than expose live references"), so it is a stale snapshot, not a live handle. The commit handler runs later and unconditionally patches `x: fit.x, y: fit.y` (editor.ts:4431-4436) computed from that snapshot; `resizeFrameToSize` is identity on x/y at rotation 0 (resize.ts:127-131), so the patch carries entry-time x/y even in the unrotated case. Both stores merge the patch over the frame present at commit time (memory.ts:708; yorkie-slides-store.ts:1456), so the entry-time x/y overwrite any position change made during the edit. I searched for a guard making that unreachable and found none: remote document changes only trigger repaint (slides-view.tsx:1107-1115) and no exitEditMode/finishEditMode call site in editor.ts (1647, 1702, 2460, 2487, 3882, 4107, 4210, 4462) is driven by a store change, so a peer moving the element while the user types is silently reverted on commit. Real, unguarded, in-lane (stale state / data overwrite), major impact.
